ratings_why.fun: The growth curve has a good shape: small copied gains early, a tree that pays out wider each tier, and Missel, Hedera and Viscum turning it quadratic late without a true loop.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because the board becomes a host tree you build, and Bloom inverts it so tiny roots like Ivy Shoots or a Bird's Egg are prized; no current tribe plays as a graph of who is on whom.

verdict_why: v3 closed the rules holes; what is left is tuning numbers, which the owner does after, not design fixes.

points.text: The early turns lean on Ivy Sprig and Woodbine only; a Tier 1 body that fights well alone before it has a host would steady turns 1-3.
Lady Hedera with Hop Bine and Missel copies every gain in full down deep chains, so growth scales with chain length squared. On target at 6 climbers, but it's the place to look if Grand Oak runs hot.
Hanger-on pays 2 gold a turn from Tier 2 once you pile three climbers on your biggest unit, which is easy to arrange; a fine hot economy piece, worth testing early.
Cousin Dodder with Old Man's Beard is a kill-and-feast chain that grows each time an enemy dies. It is bounded by enemy count, and it's a fun climax worth keeping.
Falling onto 'your biggest unit next to it' could say what happens when that unit is climbing the faller (next biggest, I assume) so the no-loops rule reads cleanly.

standouts.why: Ivy Runner feeds both the spread and the Bloom builds with Shoots that are copiers and ideal roots at once.
Ivy in Flower makes the small-host choice pay off big, and its +4/+4 cascades down chains.
Missel is a clear Tier 5 direction card: count your tree, grow the root, and shield the single point of failure.

weakest.why: Honeysuckle Tendril is a near-blank 1/2 in the turns a Tier 1 is meant to win fights.
Mistletoe Clump adds almost nothing net; it only matters as a Bloom enabler or sell trick.
Lattice Ivy is redundant once Lady Hedera lands, so it is a dead draw in the late Grand Oak.

flags.note: Full share down deep chains with Hop Bine, Missel or Viscum grows with the square of chain length.
Viscum's buff to every unit is also copied by climbers, so deep chains take it several times over.
A huge host dying early hands every falling climber a third of it; together with Cousin Dodder kills it can swing a fight hard.
2 gold a turn from Tier 2 is easy to set up; golden gives 4.
